sections.name: PARTIES AND REASONS FOR JURISDICTION.
sentences: Plaintiff, Dean Hennedy (hereinafter “Plaintiff”), is an adult individual residing at the above address.

Defendant, New Age Development Group, LLC (hereinafter “Defendant”) is a limited liability company organized and existing under the laws of Pennsylvania with a principal place of business at the above address.

sections.name: Operative Facts.
sentences: In or about August 2018, Mr. Hennedy was hired by Defendant as a project manager.
Mr. Hennedy was qualified for his position and had all the required clearances and education in order to satisfactorily complete his duties for Defendant.
Mr. Hennedy’s national origin is Egyptian but has been a United States citizen since April 17, 1980.
In or about October 2018, Defendant requested that Mr. Hennedy complete a clearance form for his employment.
That clearance form requested Mr. Hennedy’s national origin.
Mr. Hennedy listed Egyptian as his national origin.

Immediately after Mr. Hennedy returned the form to Defendant via Mr. Hennedy’s supervisor, Steven O’Reilly, Mr. O’Reilly asked if Mr. Hennedy was “an alien,” which Mr. Hennedy responded that he is a United States citizen.
Despite answering Mr. O’Reilly’s question, Mr. O’Reilly continued to call Mr. Hennedy an alien.

Mr. Reilly introduced Mr. Hennedy to a new estimator, saying, “Do you know this guy is an alien?” At Defendant’s Christmas party in 2018, Mr. Reilly introduced Mr. Hennedy to subcontractors of Defendant, saying “Can you believe this guy is an alien?” Mr. Hennedy refrained from making a complaint as Defendant is a small company and Mr. Hennedy was afraid to lose his job. In or about January 2019, after nearly six months of employment without needing a superintendent’s license, Mr. O’Reilly told Mr. Hennedy that he needed a superintendent’s license to continue working for Defendant.
Upon information and belief, no similarly situated United States born employees were required to obtain superintendent’s licenses.
Mr. Hennedy immediately began working on the process of obtaining a superintendent’s license.

On or about February 27, 2019, Mr. O’Reilly approached Mr. Hennedy and terminated Mr. Hennedy’s employment due to “lack of work.” Upon information and belief, Mr. Hennedy believes the reason for his termination was pretext because at the same time of Mr. Hennedy’s termination of employment, Defendant moved a United States born employee to replace Mr. Hennedy and hired another employee to provide estimates in Philadelphia.

As a direct and proximate result of Defendant’s conduct, Plaintiff sustained great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, as well emotional distress, humiliation, pain and suffering and other damages as set forth below.
III. Causes of Action.

sections.name: CAUSES OF ACTION.
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-26 as if fully set forth at length herein.
Defendant took adverse action against Plaintiff through its harassment and the termination of Plaintiff’s employment.

sections.name: COUNT I - TITLE VII – NATIONAL ORIGIN DISCRIMINATION
sentences: Plaintiff’s status as an Egyptian places him in a protected class.
Plaintiff’s membership in a protected class was a motivating factor in Defendant’s decision to harass and ultimately terminate his employment.

sections.name: COUNT II - VIOLATION OF THE PENNSYLVANIA HUMAN RELATIONS ACT
sentences: At all times material hereto, and pursuant to the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq, Defendant is Plaintiff’s “employer” and thereby subject to the strictures of the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act.

sentences: Defendant took adverse action against Plaintiff through its harassment and the eventual termination of Plaintiff’s employment.
Plaintiff’s status as an Egyptian places him in a protected class.

sections.name: Relief Requested.
sentences: WHEREFORE, Plaintiff, Dean Hennedy, demands judgment in his favor and against Defendant, New Age Development Group, LLC in an amount in excess of $150,000.00 together with: Compensatory damages, including but not limited to: back pay, front pay, past lost wages, future lost wages.

Lost pay increases, lost pay incentives, lost opportunity, lost benefits, lost future earning capacity, injury to reputation, mental and emotional distress, pain and suffering Punitive damages; Attorneys fees and costs of suit; Interest, delay damages; and, Any other further relief this Court deems just proper and equitable.

sections.name: TITLE VII – NATIONAL ORIGIN DISCRIMINATION
sentences: (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000e-2(a)) (Plaintiff v. Defendant) Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-26 as if fully set forth at length herein.
Defendant took adverse action against Plaintiff through its harassment and the termination of Plaintiff’s employment.
Plaintiff’s status as an Egyptian places him in a protected class.
Plaintiff’s membership in a protected class was a motivating factor in Defendant’s decision to harass and ultimately terminate his employment.
Plaintiff suffered disparate treatment by Defendant, as set forth above.

As such, Defendant’s decision to harass, treat Plaintiff differently than his Caucasian co-workers, and ultimately terminate Plaintiff’s employment is an unlawful employment practice, under 42. U.S.C. § 2000e-2(a).

As a proximate result of Defendant’s conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, as well as emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff has also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.
As a result of the conduct of Defendant, Plaintiff hereby demands punitive damages.
Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. §2000e-2(a), et seq., Plaintiff demands attorneys’ fees and court costs.

sections.name: (43 P.S. § 955)
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-35 as if fully set forth at length herein.
At all times material hereto, and pursuant to the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq, an employer may not discriminate against an employee based on national origin.
Plaintiff is a qualified employee and person within the definition of Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq,.
Defendant is Plaintiff’s “employer” and thereby subject to the strictures of the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq,.

Defendant’s conduct in harassing and terminating Plaintiff’s employment are adverse actions, were taken as a result of his national origin and constitutes a violation of the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq,.

As a proximate result of Defendant’s conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, as well as emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff has also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of his earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.
Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq Plaintiff demands attorneys’ fees and court costs.

sections.name: (42 U.S.C. § 1981)
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-42 as if fully set forth at length herein.
Defendant took adverse action against Plaintiff through its harassment and the eventual termination of Plaintiff’s employment.
Plaintiff’s status as an Egyptian places him in a protected class.
Plaintiff’s membership in a protected class was a motivating factor in Defendant’s decision to harass and ultimately terminate his employment.
Plaintiff suffered disparate treatment by Defendant, as set forth above.
Defendant took adverse action against Plaintiff by terminating his employment.
As set forth above, Plaintiff’s status in a protected class was a motivating factor in Defendant’s decision to terminate his employment.

As such, Defendants’ decision to harass, treat Plaintiff differently than his Caucasian co-workers, and ultimately terminate Plaintiff’s employment is an unlawful employment practice, under 42. U.S.C. § 1981.

As a proximate result of Defendant’s conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, as well as emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff has also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.

Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA): You may sue under the ADEA at any time from 60 days after the charge was filed until 90 days after you receive notice that we have completed action on the charge.
In this regard, the paragraph marked below applies to your case: The EEOC is closing your case.

Equal Pay Act (EPA): You already have the right to sue under the EPA (filing an EEOC charge is not required.) EPA suits must be brought in federal or state court within 2 years (3 years for willful violations) of the alleged EPA underpayment.
This means that backpay due for any violations that occurred more than 2 years (3 years) before you file suit may not be collectible.
